title: Photo Collage Cutting Off Faces? Check Each Cell’s Crop
description: If a photo collage cuts off a face, adjust that photo’s position and zoom inside its cell, then try a layout closer to the original shape.
direct: If a face is cut off, drag the photo inside its cell or zoom out. If important edges still cannot fit, choose a cell closer to the shape of the original.
figureAlt: Portrait crop outline keeps the whole face and comfortable headroom.

cards.choice.heading: Separate crop from resolution
cards.choice.body: A rectangular photo placed in a differently shaped cell may lose edges. Exporting more pixels can improve sampling, but it cannot bring back a head that was outside the chosen crop. Check composition before checking sharpness.
sections.explain.heading: When one layout cannot fit everything
sections.explain.body: A tall portrait and a wide group photo ask for different spaces. Try a different arrangement or split the collection into two images if the important subjects cannot fit. The current listing supports moving and zooming photos; it does not establish an automatic no-crop mode or a guarantee that every original edge can fit every layout.
sections.practice.heading: Inspect the final image
sections.practice.body: Our iPhone app combines 2 to 30 images in 11 layouts, with exports up to 3000 pixels wide. One export is free; further exports require Pro. Keep original photos so that an export crop remains a reversible choice. A clear crop with the right subject matters more than filling every cell with the maximum number of pictures.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: What if the face fits but the people at the sides are cut off?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Treat the group as the subject. Try a wider cell or give that image a larger panel, then recheck everyone near the edges.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Will a larger export bring back a cropped edge?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: No. More output pixels can help sharpness inside the chosen crop. Change the crop or layout to bring an edge back into view.

steps.step-1.text: Select the original photos in Combine Photos: Stitch & Grid. Choose a layout whose cell shapes suit the group.
steps.step-2.text: Drag each photo to position the important subject and adjust zoom. Check hair, chins, hands and people near the edges.
steps.step-3.text: Export a JPEG or PNG, then open the saved file in Photos or Files. Inspect every cell before sharing it.
